skeleton.description: Clone a GitHub repository, review its source code with an LLM, and create a single consolidated GitHub issue containing all findings.

state.name: validate
state.contract:
Read config.repo_url. Parse it as a https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> URL. Set ctx.data.owner and ctx.data.repo to the extracted values.
Verify preconditions in order; on the first failure set ctx.data.error to a human-readable message and emit FAIL — do no further work: 1. config.repo_url is present and matches https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> (no trailing .git required). 2. The GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable is non-empty. 3. Call GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo} with the token. - If the response is not HTTP 200, fail with the status and message from the API body. - If the response body has "has_issues": false, fail with "Repository has issues disabled." 4. Inspect the X-OAuth-Scopes response header; it must contain "repo" or "public_repo". If absent or insufficient, fail with "GITHUB_TOKEN lacks required scope."
Never write GITHUB_TOKEN to any output file or log. Emit PASS on success; emit FAIL on any precondition failure.

state.name: clone_repo
state.contract:
Build an authenticated clone URL from config.repo_url and GITHUB_TOKEN: https://<GITHUB_TOKEN>@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git Keep this URL in memory only — never write it to any file.
Run: git clone --depth 1 --single-branch <authenticated_url> <c.out()>/repo
On success write the file clone_ok.txt to c.out() (content: "ok") and emit DONE. On git failure (non-zero exit) set ctx.data.error to the last 10 lines of stderr and emit FAIL.

state.name: filter_files
state.contract:
Walk the directory tree inside the clone_repo stage output (the repo/ subdirectory).
Exclude the following unconditionally: - Directories: node_modules/, vendor/, .git/, __pycache__/, dist/, build/, .next/, coverage/ - Binary file extensions: .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .ico .webp .svg .woff .woff2 .ttf .eot .pdf .zip .gz .tar .tgz .bz2 .xz .7z .rar .exe .dll .so .dylib .bin .class .pyc - Lock files: package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, poetry.lock, Cargo.lock, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock, go.sum - Minified files: *.min.js, *.min.css, *.bundle.js - Files larger than 200 KB (204 800 bytes)
Collect relative paths (from the repo root) of all remaining files.
Group the collected files by their top-level directory component (files at the root form their own "root" group). If a group exceeds ~320 KB of aggregate source content (≈80 K tokens at 4 chars/token), split it into sub-groups of ≤320 KB each.
Set ctx.data.file_groups to an array of objects: [{ "label": "<group name>", "files": ["relative/path/to/file", ...] }, ...]
Write file_groups.json to the output directory containing the same array. Emit DONE.

state.name: review_chunk
state.contract:
You receive branchInput = { label: string, files: string[] } describing one group of source files to review, and branchIndex (the group's position in the list).
The files listed in branchInput.files are relative paths from the repository root. Read each file's content from the clone_repo stage's output directory (under repo/).
Perform a thorough code review of all provided files. For every significant finding produce a JSON object with the following fields: { "category": "security" | "correctness" | "style" | "question", "description": "<concise explanation of the issue or question>", "file": "<relative file path, or null if not file-specific>", "line": <line number as integer, or null if not applicable> }
Priorities: 1. security — vulnerabilities, exposed secrets, unsafe operations 2. correctness — bugs, logic errors, off-by-ones, unhandled errors 3. style — readability, naming, dead code, duplication (lowest priority) 4. question — ambiguous design decisions worth discussing
Rules: - Do NOT include trivial whitespace or minor formatting nitpicks. - Do NOT include findings for binary or generated files. - Do NOT invent file paths you did not read. - Every correctness/security finding MUST include a file path.
Write a single file findings.json to your output directory containing a JSON array of finding objects. If no findings exist for this group, write an empty array []. No prose outside the JSON array.

state.name: aggregate
state.contract: Read findings.json from each review_chunk branch output directory (via c.dirs('review_chunk')). Parse each file as a JSON array of finding objects. Concatenate all arrays into a single flat array, preserving every finding. Set ctx.data.total_findings to the total count of findings across all branches. Write all_findings.json to the output directory containing the merged array. Emit DONE.

state.name: compile_issue
state.contract:
Read all_findings.json from the aggregate stage's output directory.
Deduplicate: remove findings whose (category + description + file) are identical after lowercasing and trimming all three fields. Keep the first occurrence.
Sort by priority: security → correctness → style → question. Within the same category, sort alphabetically by file then by line number.
Format each finding as a numbered Markdown checklist item: N. [`file:line`] **[CATEGORY]** description (omit the file:line link component if file is null; omit the :line part if line is null)
Build the complete Markdown issue body: ## Automated Code Review Findings

 <numbered list of findings>

 ---
 *Generated on YYYY-MM-DD by automated-reviewer. Repository: ctx.data.owner/ctx.data.repo.*
If the full body string exceeds 65 000 characters, truncate the findings list (remove items from the end) until the body fits within 65 000 characters, then append: 

---
…and N more findings not shown. Set ctx.data.truncated_count to the number of omitted findings (0 if none truncated).
Compute the issue title: "Automated code review — YYYY-MM-DD" (current UTC date).
Write to the output directory: - issue_body.md — the final Markdown body string - issue_meta.json — { "title": "<title>", "owner": "<ctx.data.owner>", "repo": "<ctx.data.repo>", "truncated_count": <N> } Emit DONE.

state.name: create_issue
state.contract:
Read issue_body.md and issue_meta.json from the compile_issue stage's output directory. Read ctx.data.owner and ctx.data.repo.
Attempt to POST https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues with: { "title": issue_meta.title, "body": <contents of issue_body.md>, "labels": ["automated-review"] } Use the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Never write GITHUB_TOKEN to any file.
If the API returns 422 (label not found), retry the POST once without the "labels" field.
On HTTP 201 success: - Write issue.json to the output directory: { "url": <html_url>, "number": <number>, "owner": ctx.data.owner, "repo": ctx.data.repo } - Emit DONE.
On any other non-201 response: - Set ctx.data.error to "GitHub API error <status>: <message from response body>". - Emit FAIL.
